# Remaining training-budget evidence

Checked 17 October 2026. Research only; no application changes.

## Electrician

Use **ACC's 2026–27 Construction Management–Electrical Specialization Level 1 Certificate** as a named college preparation example. Its [award plan](https://www6.austincc.edu/cms/site/www/awardplans/awardplan.php?apid=10606&group=PCBCT&nid=31282&type=CC&year=2027) lists 25 credits across two semesters, requires an apprentice license, and describes an open-enrollment route into electrical construction.

The [current fee schedule](https://catalog.austincc.edu/college-entry/paying-for-college/tuition-rates-and-fees/) gives in-district tuition of $67/credit plus $18/credit in mandatory fees. Three required courses each carry a $50 fee in the [course catalog](https://www6.austincc.edu/cms/site/www/catalog/catalog.php?cat=2027&group=PCBCT&nid=31282&type=CC). Calculation: **25 × $85 + $150 = $2,275**. Label this “listed certificate tuition and fees,” rounded to about $2,300.

The co-op course lists an additional prerequisite, ELPT1325, absent from the award plan. Preserve this source inconsistency in developer details; the $2,275 calculation is for the listed plan, not a guaranteed final bill. Books/tools and the [$20 apprentice license](https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/electricians/apply/individuals/apprentice-electrician.htm) are separate. The certificate does not replace [journeyman supervised-work requirements](https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/electricians/apply/individuals/journeyman-electrician.htm).

Austin ETA's [published tuition](https://austineta.org/tuition-for-september-2025/) is $825 for apprentice years 1–4 in **2025–26**. The checked [2026 application page](https://austineta.org/application-deadline-for-mid-term-january-2026-classes/) does not give a new tuition figure. Keep $35 application-only; do not portray it as training cost.

## Physical therapy

UT Southwestern offers a [31-month, 96-credit DPT](https://shp.utsouthwestern.edu/programs/physical-therapy/curriculum/) qualifying graduates to sit licensing exams. Its [financial-aid budget](https://www.utsouthwestern.edu/education/students/financial-aid/cost-of-attendance/health-professions/) has resident program-year totals of $64,334, $59,382 and $33,593. Their sum is **$157,309 including living**, of which **$42,542 is tuition and fees**.

The page heading says 2026–27, but its footer dates estimates March 14, 2025. Store both. The undated [program cost page](https://shp.utsouthwestern.edu/programs/physical-therapy/costs.html) separately estimates $49,500 resident tuition, fees and books. Prefer the itemized financial-aid rows for calculations. Undergraduate preparation is additional; Dallas student living is distinct from Austin post-training living.

## Physician

[UTRGV's 2026–27 MD budgets](https://www.utrgv.edu/som/admissions/tuition-and-financial-aid/cost-of-attendance/index.htm) provide a full named Texas public example. Resident off-campus program-year totals are $61,617, $53,205, $64,585 and $61,512. Sum: **$240,919 including living**, of which **$88,398 is tuition and fees**. The [MD is four years](https://www.utrgv.edu/programs/ume-doctor-of-medicine.htm).

Use the different year rows, not four copies of the first year. This is UTRGV, not Dell Medical School. Add undergraduate preparation separately, then paid residency/fellowship. These sums hold current published budgets constant, rather than claiming a future cohort price. COA is not debt: subtract aid/contributions before calculating borrowing, and avoid adding living costs twice.

The companion JSON contains values, year rows, scope, source URLs, and limitations for direct implementation.
